From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tenant environment verification — preflight handshake

Hi Alice / Cardinal infra team,

We're starting the preflight verification for the Redwood private deployment into your tenant (CRD-4512). To keep the first pass light and unblock scheduling of the handover call, can you confirm the items below and attach any artifacts you already have?

Quick ask list (first pass):
- Network diagram showing peering (ExpressRoute / Direct Connect) or transit topology and ASN(s) used
- NAT/egress IP ranges that we should allow in the Redwood service ACLs
- Firewall rules export or a short CSV of port ranges for outbound/inbound flows to our endpoints
- Preferred TLS termination point (customer LB / Redwood service) and whether mutual TLS will be used
- KMS/HSM provider details and whether customer-managed keys are required for this deployment
- Any BGP community or route-filtering constraints we should be aware of

We're aiming to run a short connectivity smoke between 2027-05-11 and 2027-05-13 (US business hours). If that window doesn't work, suggest an alternative.

I've attached a short template for the IP allowlist we'll use on our side — if you can return a completed copy with the egress ranges that would be ideal.

Attachments: redwood-vpc-ip-allowlist.txt (template)

Next steps from our side: once we get your network diagram and IP ranges we'll:
- Validate peering requirements and produce a minimal firewall matrix for your security team
- Propose specific test IPs and temporary credentials for smoke runs
- Schedule a 45-minute walkthrough with your infra/ops and our onboarding engineers

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call to walk through anything in the list.

Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0128

[Attachment: redwood-vpc-ip-allowlist.txt (text)]

Hi Jordan —

Thanks, sending over what we have from our side. See attached: network diagram and firewall export. Quick notes:

- Connectivity: We plan private connectivity via our Azure ExpressRoute circuit (peer ASN 65123). We also use a central transit VNet; diagram indicates the spoke where your peering will terminate.
- Egress IPs: Attached fw_rules_export.csv includes the NAT translation range (10.240.200.0/24) mapped to our egress pool — please confirm whether you need the public mapped egress IPs or private ranges for your routing config.
- TLS: TLS will terminate at our front-door; we can enable mutual TLS for the Redwood service if required — need to confirm cert provisioning and rotation cadence.
- KMS: We use Azure Key Vault for key storage; customer-managed keys are supported but require SPM enrollment (I can open the ticket if we go this route).
- Change window: We have a maintenance freeze 2027-05-12 (entire day). Any smoke test should avoid that date.

Attachments: cardinal_network_diagram_v2.pdf, fw_rules_export.csv

We can do a 45-minute handover call on Monday 2027-05-10 in the afternoon (1:00–2:00 PM ET). Does that work for your engineers?

Best,
Alice Yang
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Cardinal Health
alice.yang@cardinalhealth.com

Hi Alice — thanks for the attachments and the timing note. We updated the template and have a few clarifying questions before the 5/10 walkthrough: 

1) Egress IPs: Please confirm whether the fw_rules_export.csv lists translated public egress IPs or only internal NAT ranges. For our allowlist we need the public egress addresses that your firewall NATs to (or the documented public range your outbound proxy uses).

2) TLS/mTLS: If TLS terminates at your front-door and you require mTLS, we'll need the cert thumbprint and rotation policy. If you prefer termination on Redwood, we can propose a short-lived cert flow and a small DMZ rule set — which would you prefer for initial ramp?

3) KMS/SECRETS: If you want CMK in Azure Key Vault, we'll need a KMS onboarding ticket and the service principal that will be granted wrap/unwrap permissions. If not, we can use Redwood-managed keys and provide the KMS SLA in the onboarding doc.

4) BGP/Peering: Please confirm the BGP ASN we should expect and whether there are any route filters or community tagging required. Also confirm whether the peering will be direct from your spoke VNet or via an intermediate transit appliance.

5) Service accounts & owners: Please share the owner for the service account we should expect us to use for health checks and the contact for on-call escalations.

Action items we will take before the call: 
- Produce a minimal inbound/outbound matrix compatible with your fw CSV (Marissa)
- Generate a proposed temporary test allowlist (Jordan)
- Draft an mTLS cert flow and short-lifecycle proposal (Karthik)

I've attached an updated allowlist template with a short section for "Public egress confirmed" for your ops team to fill.

Looking forward to Monday — please confirm the 1:00–2:00 PM ET slot and whether you prefer Zoom or Teams.

Marissa Cole
Technical Onboarding Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

[Attachment: redwood-vpc-ip-allowlist.txt (updated template)]
